articles.title: Crazed Porcelain
articles.summary: Micro glaze fracture web with secondary checks, glaze lips and tiny chips; subtle warped shine, low coverage. A dense scaly or chainmail-like sheen; individual hooks blur into a rippled, textured shimmer.
articles.what: A warped quadrilateral glaze fracture network contains secondary arrested checks, glaze lips, tiny pore clusters and exposed corner chips. Up close: Interlocking wavy hook shapes, 15-25 px, packed into rows like chain mail, scales or wiggly tiles. On satin only some of them flash bright in the highlight, as isolated chips; on metallic every tile shows with bevelled light edges. From a distance: A dense scaly or chainmail-like sheen; individual hooks blur into a rippled, textured shimmer. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Crack & Weather (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, trim.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Crack & Weather", or search for "Crazed Porcelain".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hero panels like hood and doors
Avoid trim where tiles get cut off
Moderate busy; bold numbers read, thin numbers get a rippled edge.
Scattered bright chips in the highlight, a sparkly scaled look
Pairs well with: gloss, metallic, matte.
pitfalls: Not a porcelain crackle: no thin crack lines are visible, the render is wavy hook tiles
Not a paint pattern: adds no white glaze colour
Avoid: very subtle, may not read at speed, low coverage leaves large clean areas.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Crazed Porcelain over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.
